text:
maya: FYI customer OrgAcme submitted an escalation: their quantized endpoint (4-bit) is both slower and producing worse text than the FP16 variant after our 4-bit rollout. They say p95 latency up ~30% and responses are hallucinating more. ticket: #ACME-927.
kevin: ugh. which runtime config and model? dedicated or hosted?
maya: Dedicated, gpu pool = r-infer-a100-40, model = open-llama-13b -> our 4bit quant build (q4_0) pinned. Autoscaling off.
sasha: can we get the exact request payload and seed? Ask support for repro inputs and a small prompt set.
support-bot: forwarded samples from customer (5 prompts). Attachments: prompt_set.txt.
anna: quick thought: 4-bit paths sometimes pay extra dequant/packing overhead on our kernel selection when sequence length is short. If their typical seq len is <128 it can flip kernel choice to scalar fallback.
kevin: yes, we've seen that. Also calibration mismatches can push quant params that blow up dynamic range and cause numeric instability -> quality drops.
maya: support says avg seq len = 64, batch size = 1 for API traffic. Throughput low but p95 high. Customer ran canned bench and saw FP16 p95=120ms, q4 p95=160ms.
leon: can you run a quick repro on our preprod using the same model config? I'll grab a trace. Command: 
```
redwood-run --model open-llama-13b:q4_0 --device gpu0 --profile perf --requests prompts.jsonl --batch 1 --seq 64
```
kevin: also try forcing kernel selection: 
```
export RWRT_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=packed_gemm_fp16,packed_gemm_q4,dequant_stream
redwood-run ...
```
leon: ran with customer's prompts. Profiling summary (top lines):
- total tokens: 420
- avg latency per token: FP16=8.6ms, Q4=10.9ms
- hotspot: layer 6-10 GEMM dequant + scatter ops increased 2.2x
- kernel chosen for Q4: fallback_scalar_dequant (not optimized vectorized kernel)
kevin: fallback_scalar_dequant is our slow-path for small seqs when packing cost > vector kernel setup. That explains latency.
sasha: what about quality? any log of logits or calibration stats?
leon: attached small table: per-layer scale stats show very skewed ranges in early layers after calibration: layer 2 scale=1e-6, layer 3 scale=1.2e2. Means quant zero-point shifting causing saturation in some heads.
anna: yep miscalibration. The calibration routine used a tiny sample from customer data that had outliers and that blew the per-channel scales. Two mitigations: re-run calibration with robust stats (use median-of-abs or clip 99.9pct), or force per-tensor fallback to INT8 for offending layers.
kevin: short-term mitigation for customer: revert endpoint to FP16 (fastest path), or pin Q4 but set runtime flag to prefer fp16 kernels for short sequences so we avoid slow scalar fallback: 
```
--runtime-override 'prefer_kernel=fp16_for_short_seq'
```
that will reduce latency at cost of more memory.
maya: Customer wants a quick fix without downtime. Can we offer a hot-config change?
sasha: yes, we can push a per-endpoint runtime override. Ops could toggle kernel preference + re-calibrate with robust sample asynchronously.
leon: I prepared a patch to kernel selector to add a cheap heuristic: if seq_len < 128 and batch ==1 prefer vectorized fp16 path unless quantized kernel measured speedup > 1.15x on that hw+model combo. Will submit PR after triage.
kevin: add a telemetry tag so we can roll back if any regression: telemetry.event = "q4_shortseq_fallback_override". Also capture kernel decision histogram.
anna: for quality, I'll generate a recalibration job: use 10k random prompts from customer traffic, clip at 99.5 percentile, and validate perplexity/regression against FP16 baseline. If pass, we can recommend re-quantize with new scales.
maya: comms: I'll tell the customer we recommend temporary rollback to FP16 or enabling the kernel preference and that we're investigating calibration and will follow up with a re-quantized image within 48h.
support-bot: I filed internal follow-up GH issue: r-infer/bugs#1482 and assigned kevin, le oncall.
kevin: action items: 1) ops: apply kernel preference override for customer endpoint (sasha) 2) calc job: anna to run robust calibration and validate 3) repo: leon to capture traces & PR for selector 4) maya to draft customer note and rollback instructions.
sasha: doing 1 now, will post confirmation.
leon: uploaded perf trace (trace_171800) and kernel decision log. Early note: 4-bit path is correct but miscalibration + small seq fallback => combined perf+quality hit.
maya: thanks team. I'll update the customer and cc this thread. Please paste any short commands or logs here so I can include them.
